first_impression.reaction: We searched 'greece wedding cost' hoping for a ballpark, and the first thing we're told is that there isn't one. That stung for a second. But the next line, 'Write down your wedding first', is the same advice I'd give a client, and nobody's trying to sell us a fairytale. So we kept going, mostly skimming the headings. James went straight to the ferry and guest accommodation bits.

journey.quote: A single figure blends all of those together and says very little about your own wedding.
journey.reaction: True, but it reads a little like a dodge when you clicked on a cost article. I'd respect it more if it said outright 'we won't give you a number here, and here's why'.

journey.section: Why there is no single Greece wedding cost
journey.quote: Send that brief to every venue and planner, so the quotes describe the same wedding.
journey.reaction: This is practical. Comparing like with like is exactly how we'd want to run this. Saves us the spreadsheet chaos.

journey.quote: Ask, too, whether another wedding can be held there the same day.
journey.reaction: I wouldn't have thought to ask that, and the idea of another bridal party in our photos is our nightmare. Feels like someone who's actually been on site.

journey.section: Season and day of the week
journey.quote: The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia does not permit weddings during several fixed periods, including the first half of August and from Great Lent until Easter Sunday.
journey.reaction: Insider detail. Not relevant to us directly, but it tells me the writer knows the calendar traps.

journey.section: The legal route and its fees
journey.quote: Originals go to the registrar two days before the wedding, and a fee applies at the registry office.
journey.reaction: Useful, but the whole legal section is a wall of text built on one island. We haven't even picked Rhodes. I skimmed most of it and came out unsure whether this applies to Santorini or Mykonos.

journey.quote: If guests are island hopping, who carries the cost of a cancelled ferry and an extra night?
journey.reaction: This is our parents and grandparents question. Glad it's asked, though I'd love to know how a Wedded Advisor actually handles it.

journey.quote: in Rhodes, you return to the registry office the next working day to sign and have the marriage certificate drawn up.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of thing that blows up a honeymoon flight booking. Exactly the hidden logistics we worry about.

journey.quote: Taxes and service charges, and whether they sit inside the quoted price.
journey.reaction: Good. Hidden costs are our biggest fear and this list is honest about where they hide.

journey.section: Euro quotes and the Australian dollar
journey.quote: If you pay in euro, each payment's cost in AUD depends on the exchange rate on the day it leaves your account, so ask your bank how it charges for international transfers and allow for the rate to move.
journey.reaction: Addresses the currency fear directly. Paired with the AUD quoting line later, this is the most reassuring part of the page.

journey.quote: When a service has a major problem, you can cancel and get a refund, which may not be in full because you pay a reasonable amount for work already done, or keep the contract and pay a lower price.
journey.reaction: As a lawyer I appreciate the care, but this is the point my partner would stop reading. It's long, and it doesn't tell me who is accountable if something goes wrong on the day in Greece.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and has inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This is the line that actually matters to us, and it's buried at the end of a legal section. It should be easier to find.

journey.quote: It depends on the wedding you plan. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total.
journey.reaction: Second time I've been told 'it depends'. In an FAQ this feels evasive, even if it's honest.

journey.section: Planning your Greece wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing upfront is a good sign. 'One' person is what we want. But every planner says this, and I still don't know what happens on the day or whether vendors are people they know.

unanswered_questions: Is there any range at all, even a rough one, so we know whether our budget is realistic for Greece before we spend weeks writing a brief?
Does the Wedded Advisor come to Greece for the wedding, or who is our accountable person on the day?
Does Wedded Wonderland work with suppliers it knows in Greece, or are vendors sourced fresh for each wedding?
How does a Wedded Advisor handle guest transfers from the airport to the venue, especially for older guests?
Do the civil wedding steps described for Rhodes apply on Santorini, Mykonos or Crete?
Is there a real Greece wedding (venue and date) we can look at?
How is the planner fee worked out, even roughly?

turn_offs_found.quote: It depends on the wedding you plan. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total.
turn_offs_found.why: Vague pricing with no ranges is one of our turn-offs. A cost article with no figures at all, repeated in the FAQ, feels like it's holding back.

would_share_with: Partner (the getting around and guest accommodation sections)
Parents, since they're contributing (the packages inclusions list and the paying from Australia section)

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge, and for more ideas, read the Get Wedded magazine.
cta_reaction.why: It's low pressure, which we like. But we'd normally read a couple more posts and see a real wedding first, and this page doesn't link to one. The AUD quote and written fee are the pull; the missing day-of accountability is the hold-back.

top_3_changes: Own the no-number stance in the intro instead of implying it. OLD: "A single figure blends all of those together and says very little about your own wedding." NEW: "A single figure blends all of those together and says very little about your own wedding, so this guide doesn't give one. It gives you the questions that turn each quote into something you can compare."

Make the FAQ answer feel less evasive. OLD: "It depends on the wedding you plan. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total." NEW: "It depends on the wedding you plan, and a headline number rarely survives a real guest list. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total, so the fastest route to a figure you can trust is one written brief sent to each venue."

Add the accountability question we actually lie awake over. OLD: "- What happens if a ferry is cancelled or the weather turns on the day?" NEW: "- What happens if a ferry is cancelled or the weather turns on the day?\n- Who is our point of contact on the wedding day, and who is accountable if a supplier lets us down?"

open_questions.question: A cost post with no figures at all is this persona's main objection. Is there sourced, Nic-approved range material that could be added in a later round, or should the post explicitly frame itself as a no-figures guide?
Can a real Greece wedding (venue and date) be linked from this post? This persona usually needs one before enquiring.
